content.text: If we don’t bring migrated postings, then we will face the following issues:

Period end balance will not be useful for migrated contracts as there will be no opening balance for balance sheet GLs on the cutover date. Even prospectively in the 2nd period after migration, the opening balance will not be true reflection of transactions occurred in the past because of not catering impact of historical journal entries despite such entries exist in our ledger transactions in NLA 6.x.

When the migrated contract inception (re-recognition) posting will be there in period end balances because such posting is local posting, then it will create wrong reporting and can create audit issues if client depend on such report because it will not be able to nullify impact of migration re-recognition entries, because of the absence of termination posting.
I believe we shall work on such enhancement as a phase 2 approach to period end balance where we shall bring in not only termination posting but also all historical postings.

content.text: Root cause: The audit log export needs a DB stored procedure that is missing in the affected environment.

shows the database was copied. A DB copy or migration does not copy stored procedures; they are only created during application deployment. Because the procedure is missing, the export fails for all object types and all date ranges.
On a freshly deployed 2026.R2 build (local), the export works correctly, so the product code is fine.
Mike Hu confirmed the stored procedure does not exist in the copied DB.

content.text: In 5.x, Finning was able to enable a posting sequence that prevented users from posting transactions out of order.
In version 6.x, two workarounds were provided:
Posting based on the Activation Group ROU Start Date
– This workaround enables users to post missed transactions from prior periods. However, it does not prevent transactions from being posted out of sequence.
– This feature helps prevent posting issues by restricting postings to the appropriate accounting periods, thereby reducing the risk of out-of-sequence transactions.
Finning requires the Posting sequence feature in 6.x.

content.text: In the absence of an authorized profile for a user, access to details on landing pages or jobs is restricted. However, the issue observed in the screenshot appears to be because the user possessing both "nla_admin" and "nla_security" roles. To fix this, we recommend retrying the login with NLA roles excluding the above two.

Moving forward, when a user logs into NLA without the necessary roles, instead of displaying blank pages, the product will be enhanced to prompt/notify the user to create a user profile for complete access to the NLA product.

Furthermore, while investigating this issue, additional issues were identified. Even in cases where no profiles are assigned, users are able to execute certain actions. These underlying issues will also be addressed as part of this ticket.
Able to view the export and import jobs list
Able to create Profiles under Batch Management and Reporting module
Able to create default value configs
Able to view and download from previous history of reports

content.text: The reported issue occurs when the user is able to close the Lease Component (LC) while an associated Activation Group (AG) is still active, which should not be allowed.

The Close option for a Lease Component should be disabled if there is any associated AG that is not in a Closed or Discarded status. This restriction ensures consistency by preventing users from closing the LC while an AG is still active or pending.

Currently, because the LC Close button is enabled regardless of the AG status, users can inadvertently close the LC, which disrupts the contract’s lifecycle and prevents further processing. This leads to unintended closure states that impact contract functionality.
Able to reproduce the issue on internal Master build
Active Type of LC is Closed
Create and Activate - MA, CT, LC and AG
Create LC modification event and AG modification event on ROU Start Date
Create LC modification event and access AG
Revert the Active Type of AG
Issue: After Revert action - New AG is created and is still in Active Status
Access LC and check the Workflow components
User is able to close the LC

fields.summary: NRE Dep: Tax (Including Vendor Split)

content.text: The assessment provided for the bullet points in the description (Requirements) includes observations, furthermore FAQs to facilitate the concerned ones.
Dev provided the overview of the new schedules view as per the guidelines of the product team and made changes in their build, which is at the Prod-Validation / Acceptance stage now.
For this requirement, a detailed evaluation is provided in
. However the crux of the assessment is that, user can do the manual postings for both IFRS and US GAAP but batch posting function is failing the job.

Tax functionality is working properly, as it ask for to calculate taxes checkbox at contract level. At LC level under the heading of payment spilt, asking for the percentage charge to the partner, tax jurisdiction, tax code and exempt amount.
The issue is in the tax journals, placing the SS to show the current journals, however suggestion at the end of assessment is provided:
, converting the tax amounts into company currency (CAD) & group currency (USD) but not for the payment journals, though exchange rates fetched from FOS are correct.
The daunting thing is, multiplying the contract currency with exchange rate for
to get the amounts in group currency. Means instead of multiplying the 87.750 * 1 which is equals to 87.750 (USD amount), doing 65.000 * 1 = 65.000.
However not converting the contract currency to company and group currency respectively at accrual postings
Suppose that a lease contract have a lease term of 12 months, receiving the lease rentals at the start of month. In that case the payment journals  should hit the
(Credit). For example having an accrued rent income of 1,000 and accrued non-lease income of 500, and applicable tax rate is 30% on both lease and non-lease amounts, the journals will be as below:
For comprehensive view attaching an excel file, to show the lessor’s journal for the full lease term:
Q: What does mean by the tax calculation on gross and net basis?

A: Tax calculation - net and gross tax calculation are two different methods used in SAP to determine the amount of taxes that should be calculated and paid on a transaction. The difference between the two methods is that; in net tax calculation, the tax amount is calculated by deducting the subtotal of the transaction from the grand total - Net tax amount = grand total - subtotal. In the gross tax calculation the tax amount is calculated based on the subtotal of the transaction before adding it to the grand total - Gross tax amount = subtotal * tax rate
Q: How the NFS is fetching data regarding tax jurisdiction & Tax code determination. Is it either sync from the SAP or user have to manually enter it on FOS?
A: Both, they are ERP objects - so are contained within the SAP sync, however the user has the ability to manually create jurisdiction or codes in FOS.
Q: From where at FOS a user can edit, link or detach a tax jurisdiction (FOS link)?

content.text: Live and Data retention records - OOB values (5.x)
In 5.x we are using OOB values as - 100000 or 30 days which ever comes first
And Remove old rolling backup after - 30 days (Store as CSV files and retain for 30 Days)
Sandeep mentioned that - Pfizer has come up with issue asking for configuration and extraction of Audit logs for 6 months of data
is the only customer using the Threshold value of 5 million or 3650 days ( Configurable) ( Big sizing on AWS)
As part of this enhancement, user should be able to view the
Active logs data for 30days or 1 million records
which ever is the earliest. And user should have the ability to export the data for
User should have the ability to apply additional filters on Entity Name and Field Name as per the initial meeting A

content.text: After further internal reviews and discussions, we’ve decided not to move forward with ticket
(Migration & Parity: Year-Based Number Ranges and Last Generated ID for NLA 6X).

While this is a parity item, the feature is not a blocker for client IFRS16/ASC842 compliance, and some clients who were using it in NCP2 successfully went live on NCP3 without requiring it or raising any concerns. Based on this, we’re comfortable closing out the ticket at this time.
We will also make sure this is clearly documented in the customer-facing materials, noting that this feature is no longer part of the product.
If this topic resurfaces in the future with a specific client need, it will be re-evaluated by the product team.

content.text: There is no such thing as a non-early buy out. If the PO is exercised, it means lessee and lessor have agreed on transferring the ownership to the lessee on the PO payment date, so there is no point to continue paying base rent and not transferring the ownership to the lessee.
However, we have heard that some customer from 5.x asked for it so we will reach out to that customer to get their actual use case in order to inspect if there is actual business usage.
For now, I am putting this ticket on hold till we have some solid information on why we need this.

fields.summary: NLA: Enhance ID field Search Visibility on all Jobs and Profile listing pages (Reporting Module, Batch Management

content.text: NLA: Enhance ID field Search Visibility on all Jobs and Profile listing pages (Reporting Module, Batch Management

Currently, when a user performs a search in the search filter, the entered value is hidden, making it difficult for users to verify the search query. To enhance user-friendliness and usability, we should make the entered search term visible to the user. This can be achieved by displaying the search term in the search field prominently.

By showing the search term, we minimize the risk of unintended or erroneous searches, which can save time and prevent data-related issues. This change aligns with our commitment to providing a user-friendly interface, enhancing overall user satisfaction.
The ID entered by the user should be visible in the search field after a search is performed.

content.text: The asset replacement scenario typically refers to situations where an existing leased asset is replaced with a new one during the lease term.
This functionality should be available at the AG level.
The pop-up screen should have the fields as shown above.
SAP asset class isn’t required anymore.
Based on the replacement date, retrieve the asset and liability values in all currencies.
If we can calculate asset and liab. balances on any selected replacement date, users should be allowed to select any date
However, if can’t calculate asset and liab. balances on any selected replacement date, users should be allowed to select either period start or end date
Amounts should be retired from the old cost objects.
Amounts should be booked under new cost objects.
No financial impact should be displayed on the schedule
Both old and new cost objects should be reflected at the unit level.
If possible, reports in the historical period should reference the cost objects associated with the units.
Please refer to the attached document for more information on how it works in NLA 5X.
We should also consider mass way of asset replacement as well in the future
Asset replacement occurs when a unit within the activation group is returned to the lessor and replaced in kind.

e.g. I sign a lease contract for 10 taxi cabs; within the lease contract it is agreed that the lessor will provide a replacement in the case of a redundancy of one of the taxi cabs. At some point during the lease, one of the taxi cab’s is involved in a collision; the taxi cab is still operable but has damage to the paneling. As a result, I return the damaged taxi cab back to the lessor, who in turn provides a replacement.
Asset replacement was specifically designed for WM usage in 4.1 version. This allowed them to transfer the asset and liability balances to new cost objects - which they are unable to do otherwise.
During initial discussions with WM SA it was concluded that they also need this functionality for that purpose; alongside WM NA when they move onto 6.0.
In 5.x there are two types of asset replacement;
Where the asset is replaced in kind, there are no alterations to any inputs and no financial impact
The user selects the unit that is to be replaced
User provides a replacement date - which is used as the Unit End Date
Unit Status is updated from ‘Active’ to ‘Replaced’
The Reception Date is used as the ‘Activation Date’
Same Asset ID number is copied from the original replaced unit.
Where the asset is replaced in kind and there are alterations to inputs relating to the unit & a financial affect.
User initiates an Asset Replacement event (modification reason at AG level)
Upon selection the following fields should be displayed within the component
User selects the asset being replaced
User defines the asset class of the new asset
User selects the asset cost center to be used for the new asset
User selects the asset profit center to be used for the new asset
User selects the liability cost center to be used for the new asset
User selects the liability profit center to be used for the new asset
The aim for the asset replacement posting is to clear the long and short term lease payable balances from the old cost centers and move the balances under the new cost centers.
This is done via two Liability documents being created - one for Long Term Payable, the other for Short Term Payable.
The outstanding amounts in both the Long/Short Term Lease Payable accounts at the time of the Replacement Date are that which should be displayed in the documents
Contract event - changing CC should not transfer asset and liability balances
If they want to transfer - they do asset replacement
What if you change the asset class - which has a useful life of less than the original? or less than the ROU - what happens? what is the financial impact?
What amount is transferred? just the principal balances, or just the total as of the replacement date? Check with Zeina
Gross transfers - closing GBV & closing acc dep
Specific Scenario - this item will be examined for delivery post NFS 2023.R1 but possibly before NFS 2023.R2 - it may warrant its own delivery release.
This is a particular case of asset replacement at unit level where the cost centers or profit centers are changing  (see description).
No operational workaround identified currently. Possibilities include contract transfer or other complex operations which are not deemed viable.

Vet impact of not supporting this particular case with Walmart SA project team. Recommendation is to manage this with customer until it can be delivered. Delivery vehicle TBD based on vetting but will be in 2023H2 after NFS 2023.R1

content.text: Bulk asset replacement functionality will not be implemented unless requested by the customer or if issues arise in the future.
Changing Cost Object information and Asset Transfer (Cost object with Balance transfer) will be implemented separately in another enhancement phase.
These changes will not be included in the current phase focused on unit replacement.
: Users with NLA_LeaseAdmin , NLA_Accountant and NLA_Approver should have the authority to perform Unit replacement

content.text: What to do about those clients who have configured Non-Lease Expense and Non-lease Accrual in GL account mapping?
We shouldn’t be running any script. If clients have configured under GL account mapping, then they shall be communicated after this change.
, this point will be important for user guide.
What do they need to do?

Delete non-lease expense and non-lease accrual from GL account mapping and configure it to expense category mapping for non-lease expense and for non-lease accrual, configure it either under non-lease accrual account in the expense category or in non-lease accrual default account in the default account category.
What if they don’t delete existing configured non-lease expense and non-lease accrual accounts from GL account mapping?

The application shall use its new logic of looking in new placeholders of expense category or default account and if no accounts are found in such placeholders, it shall throw the error message that ‘no accounts are configured in expense category or default category for non-lease accrual and expense category for non-lease expense’.

fields.summary: [NFS] Calendar type in contract creation should check the the company code fiscal year variant

content.text: The application is allowing the user select wrong Calendar type making wrong periods for the document  in NLA.

In case the user select Regular Calendar for a non Calendar company code, the application generates the schedules with wrong periods and it will not match with SAP document. The example below the company code is 1003 with non calendar fiscal year variant ( V9 → Set-Aug), in this case September is the first period and with year shift +1.
In SAP the fiscal year variant V9 is non calendar with the following periods:
Add the validation for Calendar Type, when the company has a fiscal year variant not regular calendar, the user should not be able to select Calendar type
Create a contract for company code 1003.
On Accounting page select the Calendar type (Regular Calendar should not be allowed for companies where the fiscal year variant is on-calendar)
Activate the contract and check the post, if the posting periods from NLA matches with SAP.

content.text: After further internal reviews and discussions, we’ve decided not to move forward with ticket
(Migration & Parity: Year-Based Number Ranges and Last Generated ID for NLA 6X).

While this is a parity item, the feature is not a blocker for client IFRS16/ASC842 compliance, and some clients who were using it in NCP2 successfully went live on NCP3 without requiring it or raising any concerns. Based on this, we’re comfortable closing out the ticket at this time.
We will also make sure this is clearly documented in the customer-facing materials, noting that this feature is no longer part of the product.
If this topic resurfaces in the future with a specific client need, it will be re-evaluated by the product team.

content.text: After further internal reviews and discussions, we’ve decided not to move forward with ticket
(Migration & Parity: Year-Based Number Ranges and Last Generated ID for NLA 6X).

While this is a parity item, the feature is not a blocker for client IFRS16/ASC842 compliance, and some clients who were using it in NCP2 successfully went live on NCP3 without requiring it or raising any concerns. Based on this, we’re comfortable closing out the ticket at this time.
We will also make sure this is clearly documented in the customer-facing materials, noting that this feature is no longer part of the product.
If this topic resurfaces in the future with a specific client need, it will be re-evaluated by the product team.

content.text: Remove "None" Dropdown Option from Left Navigation Menu

Currently, under the "Determinations and Configurations" section, there is a dropdown titled "None" that does not contain multiple subsections. This dropdown option serves no functional purpose and may cause confusion for users.

content.text: We have added 2 different switches for PMI. Once we have ERP Field Mapping for General, we need to disable those 2 switches from the application, and also someone needs to do mapping manually for PMI.
These features will be developed in multiple phases.
is to enable the user to map any field from the application and store it at the GL level. Without having the field at the GL level, it cannot send it to SAP.
will be the basic one where customers cannot select the “FROM” fields. These fields are predefined in the application, and they can only be mapped to SAP BAPI at the header and item levels.
will be the advanced one, where customers can see multiple fields in the “FROM” field and map them to a single SAP field at the header or item level.

will be more advanced than Phase 2, where customers can map multiple fields from the application to a single SAP field at the header and item levels, also allow the customer to write a JavaScript code for each mapping.

Payment Terms: All the Payment terms should have this name
Taxes: Calculated sales taxes should have this name

When there is an indexation event with a casualty event on the same date the asset retirement document produced is incorrect.
Also, It picks the GBV prior to the index event instead of the GBV after the index event which is wrong means build is not taking the effect of the event-1
Create a 12- month lease with 2 events in the during of the lease.
-Casualty both to be performed on the same day
The build Picks the GBV before the event at casualty. Dev needs to Debug the route cause.
The system should pick the new GBV that is after event 1, for the asset retirement documents after casualty.

fields.summary: QLT: Block extensions after exercising PO/TO

content.text: The system doesn’t generate a warning message to the user if the extension option is exercised after the exercise of the termination option (TO) or purchase option (PO).
Purview of testing & behavior of application:
The NLA 6.0 is tested by performing three different sets of scenarios within the scope of this ticket.

In a lease contract in which the purchase option is exercised at the inception level, later on, the user exercised the extension option through an event and made no change to the purchase option status. The application doesn’t consider and generate any financial impact of the extension option exercised because the asset will transfer to the lessee before the extension period. The behavior of the application is correct in this regard except for the concerns explained below.

In another lease scenario, in which the termination option is exercised at inception, and through lease modification, the supplemental base rent was exercised through an AG event. The application doesn’t consider the modification and neither generated the financial impact of lease modification after the termination date, which is a correct behavior except for the concerns explained below.

In the third scenario, a lease contract is initiated with a single base rent, an extension option of 12 months, and a purchase option, however, at inception, only BR is exercised. At a later stage both the remaining terms (Extension and PO) are exercised together, system gives preference to PO over the extension option, which is correct in this case, except for the concern explained below.

The system should generate a warning message at the AG level if the termination or purchase option is exercised previously and the user is going to add the extension option, supplemental base rent, or reductions that will affect the financial schedules after the effective date of purchase or termination option. So the user should be aware of the situation that, these terms will not be entertained by the system.
The System should give the following warning message:
“There will be no financial impact and it is advised to unexercised the T.O or P.O before exercising any term that have payment date after the retirement date”.

content.text: Resolved in the FOS UI (MasterData page, which is used by the Master Data, Configuration and Determination screens). No backend or data changes.

1. Vertical resize: the gap between the records grid and the relations grid can now be dragged up or down to give either grid more height. Each grid keeps a minimum height so its toolbar, column headers, some rows and pagination always stay visible. Higher "Records per page" settings are now usable. Screens without relations are unchanged.

2. Collapsible navigation: a round toggle button on the right border of the left navigation panel collapses it to a thin strip and expands it again. Open sections and the selected ERP system are kept.

3. Per-tab layout: each tab remembers its own split and collapsed state. New tabs always open with the default layout (50/50 split, navigation expanded). The layout resets to the default after a page reload.
The existing horizontal resize between the relation tabs and the relations grid is unchanged.

fields.summary: FOS UX: Enable vertical resizing of the records/relations panels and collapsing of the side navigation panel on Determination screens

content.text: Meeting A is not required, as the implementation requirements are already clear. We will proceed directly with the implementation and move to Meeting D.
Khoi Pham (presenter), Vanessa Bui-Quang, Bhavin Topiwala, Asad Khalid, Namandeep, Touseef, Zeina
Follow-up to FCO-388, covering the UX items that were scoped out of it. The demo was on the Determination screens, such as the Lessee Carry Determination.
The left navigation panel is always expanded and takes up horizontal space, even when the user doesn’t need it.
The user can resize the relations grid horizontally, but can’t control the height split between the records grid (top) and the relations grid (bottom).
With larger page sizes (20, 50, 100 records), only a few rows are visible at the default size.
Vertical resize between the two grids
Hovering over the gap shows a resize cursor, and the divider can be dragged up or down.
Khoi and Asad decided that dragging stops at a limit where at least one row of the other grid stays visible. This stops the user from losing track of the collapsed grid.
Pagination (20, 50, 100 records) works with the new sizes, and scrolling still works as expected.
A new toggle button collapses and expands the left navigation panel, and the arrow icon flips direction with the state.
The existing menu selection (such as Master Data) is preserved.
The button changes color on hover.
Each new Determination tab opens with the default layout. Changes made in one tab (panel heights, collapsed navigation) don’t carry over to others.
The user can drag the horizontal divider between the records grid and relations grid.
The user can collapse the left navigation panel.
Resize and collapse state is consistent across Determination tabs.
The existing horizontal resize behavior is preserved.
Hover color of the collapse button (Vanessa):
The dark blue hover is too dark. A hover state should be visibly different from the default but sit in between, not go that dark. Agreed outcome:
reuse the hover color from the existing collapse button in the other product area (the one Vanessa showed on screen)
so it stays consistent with the design system. Vanessa called this minor.
Minimum one visible row when dragging to the extreme:
rather than hiding a grid completely. Hiding it fully would make users forget the grid exists, and one row gives a visual cue and still frees up a lot of space.
No other concerns. Vanessa said everything else looks good, and Asad confirmed “all good.”
Khoi: update the collapse button hover color to match the existing collapse button’s hover style elsewhere in the app.

fields.summary: Enforce SAP Field Validation for ERP Integration Data

content.text: We initially planned to restrict each field's length to match SAP requirements and avoid potential issues with future features. However, implementing this restriction could cause problems for existing clients whose current values exceed the expected length.
This is a significant concern because, once a value is changed, reports may continue to display the old value for several months before reflecting the updated value.
Given the complexity and potential impact, we have decided not to enforce these restrictions at this time. We will put the ticket on hold and revisit it in the next release.

content.text: This issue was caused by the hierarchy fields moving from ContractDto to ContractRevisionDto.

Previously, Lease Department and Lease Group were mapped directly on the Contract during Excel import. After the hierarchy fields were moved to the Contract Revision level, the UPDATE import path was updated to map these fields to the revision, but the CREATE import path was missing the equivalent revision mappings.

Because of that, during Contract CREATE import, the Excel values for Lease Department and Lease Group were not carried into the initial revision. When default-field-value processing ran, it treated those fields as not supplied and applied the configured editable defaults.

content.text: Root cause: LedgerEntriesGrid.vue's formatToDecimalPointsFromFos() needs currency.decimalPoints to render the Transaction Currency column. The amount itself was always correct (verified via live console/network debugging) — only the formatting silently failed and fell through to blank/-.

Why it was missing: LedgerTransaction's persisted CurrencyDetail (id, displayId, definitionType, currencyType) never stored decimalPoints — that's FOS master data, correctly not duplicated into transactional storage. The frontend built voucher.currency/generalInfo.currency straight from that lean object, so it never had decimalPoints on fetch or after save.

Fix — backend: added a currency field (CurrencyLite) to LedgerTransactionDto, resolved via erpMasterDataProxyService.getCurrencyById(...) in both LedgerTransactionService.get() (fetch) and JournalVoucherService.setInitialData() (create/update) — the same "resolve id → Lite object via FOS proxy" pattern already used elsewhere in this codebase (confirmed by auditing other report DTOs and the existing Company/Second/Third Currency resolution path, which goes through the identical erpMasterDataProxyService/cross-schema JDBC mechanism).
Fix — frontend: initInputs() now consumes ledgerTransaction.currency directly instead of hand-building a lean object from currencyDetail.
Root cause of the original ask: isChangedVoucher used cloneDeep + JSON.stringify is bad?

Redesign: replaced the whole clone/stringify/exclusion-list mechanism with a single reactive isDirty boolean, set by a deep: true watcher on voucher, reset at the same points the code used to re-snapshot. Retired originalVoucher, cloneVoucherWithoutVolatileFields(), removeEmptyStrings(), and the FIXME-flagged voucher.currency duplication.
Three timing bugs surfaced after that redesign, all Vue watcher-scheduling races, fixed in sequence:
a. Deep watcher used Vue's default batched ('pre') flush, so it fired after the code that reset isDirty, undoing the reset — fixed with flush: "sync".

b. Even with sync flush, other pre-existing watchers (e.g. the company watcher, still on default flush) fired in a later microtask and re-dirtied the voucher after the reset — fixed by deferring all 6 reset points with $nextTick(), so they run after Vue's pending watcher queue fully drains.

content.text: ERP System, System Config and General Settings share one `MasterData` page and swap per-tab cached state.

When the grid's columns change on a tab switch, `NakRangeInputDatePicker` mounts and immediately emits an empty value. `updateObjectFilter` treated this as a real filter change and fired a reload that:
was not bound to any tab, so its result was written to whichever tab was current when it resolved, and
still sent `erpSystemIdEqual` from the previous tab's ERP selection, which returns 0 rows for General Settings (not ERP-specific).

Skip no-op filter changes: `isFilterChanged()` treats null / `""` / `{from: null, to: null}` as equal. Object and relation filters still store the value (the date picker needs it) but only reload on a real change.
ERP filter only for ERP-specific types: `requestObjects` sends `erpSystemIdEqual` only when `selectedMetainfo.erpSystemWise`.

Bind reloads to their tab: `requestObjects` / `requestRelations` default `loadCtx` to `currentTabLoadCtx()`, so filtering, paging and table refreshes write to the tab that started them, even if the user switches tabs before the response arrives. The now-dead "no context" branches are removed.

content.text: The entity that System Config opens on changed with the UI language:
French / Spanish → Lessor Expense Category Account Mapping

defaultMasterDataEntity in stores/master_data.js sorted the determinations by their translated caption and took the first one. The mapping's French ("Correspondance…") and Spanish ("Asignación…") captions sort before "Détermination…" / "Determinación…", so it became the default in those languages.

Sort by the backend order defined in NakisaDeterminationDefinitions (with type as the tie-breaker) instead of caption. Neither field is translated, so the default is the same in every language. Accounting Standard Determination has order = 1; it is the only determination with that value, and all 28 determinations set order explicitly.

fields.summary: AG Status/Budget Inconsistency During Concurrent Activation (Race Condition)  Summary

content.text: I have tested this ticket by following the provided test scenario.
A new budget of 30,000 was created, and a contract was created and assigned to the same budget. An LC was then created with a base rent of 2,100 for a duration of 12 months.
To validate the concurrency scenario, two users attempted to activate the same AG simultaneously. The AG was activated successfully, and the expense was posted correctly without any duplication.
No duplicate expense entries were generated.
No AG remained stuck in Reprocess status.
The Inception amount is correctly reflected as 25,062.65.
The same expense amount is accurately reflected in the budget at both the Contract and MLA levels.
Based on the above validation, the functionality is working as expected and the issue is resolved.
It requires new API on NIM to check whether the budget expense is already posted or not.

content.text: I have tested this scenario both manually and through contract import, and the validations are working as expected.
MLA budgets have a different Business Unit (BU) and/or Company Code than the contract.
Expected behavior: The budget should not cascade to the contract, or a validation message should be displayed when the user clicks Send to Approval.
During contract import, the system correctly prevents the association and displays the following validation error:
"Budget (ID: BUD00000049) has Company (ID: 1000), which does not match the Contract Company (ID: 2000)."
During manual testing, the budget is no longer available for selection when its Company Code does not match the contract's Company Code, which is the expected behavior.
Based on the above testing, the validation is functioning correctly in both manual and import scenarios, and the ticket can be considered passed.

customfield_12301.value: Missing Functionality / Perceived Bug or Gap

content.text: I have tested this ticket and confirmed that the validation is working correctly for both manual MLA creation and Mass Import MLA scenarios.
When an MLA has a different Lease Department than the assigned Budget, the Budget is not displayed, which is the expected behavior.
After correcting and aligning the MLA Lease Department with the Budget Lease Department, the Budget becomes visible and can be selected.
The same behavior has been verified through Mass Import MLA and is functioning correctly.
When there is a department mismatch, the application displays the expected validation message:
Budget (ID: BUD00000048) has Lease Department (ID: DE002), which does not match the Master Agreement Lease Department (ID: DE001).
Additionally, if an MLA does not have a Lease Department assigned, the Lease Department filter is skipped as expected, and the Budget remains available for selection.
All tested scenarios are working as intended and align with the expected business requirements.
needs to be fixed before proceeding to add the Lease Department filter.

content.text: As confirmed by the Product team, Country was initially an optional field and was made mandatory in 2024 as part of a separate ticket. As a result, some existing records may not have a country assigned.

Previously, for the Tax Code and Tax Jurisdiction entities, country selection was allowed only when the record was in the Created status. This prevented users from assigning a country to existing Active or Decommissioned records.

To address this limitation, the editability condition has been updated from status.name === 'CREATED' to status.name !== 'ACTIVE'. Country selection is now allowed for records in any status other than Active. Users can temporarily change an Active record's status to Decommissioned, update the country, and then reactivate the record by changing its status back to Active.
